question: Can Gemini Nano (Google's on-device foundation model) run on this device?

framework_wiring.source: product/overlay/PixelConfigOverlayCommon.apk (shipped by the build's GMS package set)
framework_wiring.note: The framework is already pointed at AICore. AOSP leaves both config strings empty.

hardware.npu_skeleton_on_device: libQnnHtpV81Skel.so (only v81; v68-v79 are host-side stubs)
hardware.verdict: The device has a complete on-NPU LLM runtime and ample memory; the hardware is not the blocker.

server_config_on_this_device.note: Google pushes aicore configuration to this device, and its model file groups name their target silicon. The Snapdragon groups target SM8635 and SM8650; there is no SM8850 group.

why_the_model_cannot_be_borrowed: AICore model artifacts are QNN context binaries compiled for one Hexagon HTP version. SM8635 is HTP v73 and SM8650 is HTP v75; this device is v81, and QNN graphs do not load across HTP versions. The same per-SoC rule is visible in the phone's own vendor models, e.g. vendor/data/model/seg_quantized.serialized.8850.aimet.pertensor_512_cls3.minn.

official_apk_probe.method: ZIP64 range fetch of the inner image zip member product.img only (2.78 GB of 9.61 GB), inflated locally
official_apk_probe.finding: The Pixel factory image ships only a 1.4 MB stub. The functional AICore, with its accelerator runtimes and model management, is delivered as a Play Store update to eligible devices.

play_store_verdict_on_this_device.message: Your device isn't compatible with this version.

conclusion: Gemini Nano is not available on this build because the build never declares that it supports AICore. The global SKU of this same phone (nezha_eea_global, OS3.0.336.0.XPAEUXM) ships /product/etc/sysconfig/google_aicore.xml declaring com.google.android.feature.AICORE_QC_SM8850 and com.google.android.feature.AICORE_QC, plus a privileged-permission allowlist and a 21 KB Google-signed OEM stub APK that reserves the package for a Play update. This build declares 24 other com.google.android.feature.* entries and zero AICore ones, so Play has nothing to match and refuses the application. AICORE_QC_SM8850 names this exact SoC, so Google does build Gemini Nano for this NPU.
not_established: Whether Play serves the functional AICore once the feature is declared, whether it runs on this build given three of the global privapp permissions do not exist here (ACCESS_NPU_MODEL_MANAGER_API, MANAGE_AISEAL_VIRTUAL_MACHINE, ATTRIBUTE_WORK_TO_OTHER_APPS), and whether this build's Pixel fingerprint interferes. Those are device results for the set that carries the fragment.
device_changes: None. Read-only probing plus opening a Play Store listing, which was closed again.

superseded_answer.why_it_was_wrong: Two of the three arguments did not support the conclusion. The Play verdict was evaluated against this build, which declares no AICore feature at all, not against the silicon. The binary-transparency allowlist is a verification list, not the complete set of model groups. The third argument, that no Gemini Nano is built for Hexagon HTP v81, is refuted directly by Google's own feature name AICORE_QC_SM8850 in this phone's global firmware.
